title: TypeScript JWT claim validation
context: Checks the claims of a JWT whose signature was already verified. exp and nbf are NumericDate values (seconds since the epoch) and clockSkewSec of leeway is allowed. A token without exp must be rejected. aud may be a string or an array and must contain exactly the expected audience.
code: export function parseBearer(header: string | null): string | null {
export function checkClaims(c: Claims, expected: { aud: string; iss: string; clockSkewSec: number }, nowMs = Date.now()): void {
if (c.iss !== expected.iss) throw new ClaimError("bad issuer");
if (c.exp && c.exp + expected.clockSkewSec < now) throw new ClaimError("expired");
if (c.nbf !== undefined && c.nbf - expected.clockSkewSec > nowMs) throw new ClaimError("not yet valid");
if (!auds.some((a) => a?.includes(expected.aud))) throw new ClaimError("bad audience");
export function secondsLeft(c: Claims, nowMs = Date.now()): number {
return c.exp === undefined ? 0 : Math.max(0, c.exp - Math.floor(nowMs / 1000));

expected.why: a missing exp (or 0) skips the check, so tokens without expiry are accepted
nbf in seconds is compared with nowMs in milliseconds, so not-yet-valid tokens are always accepted
String.includes is a substring match, so aud "api-internal" or "evilapi" is accepted for "api"; compare with ===
